what: Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells servers, storage and networking to businesses, along with the GreenLake service that rents that hardware by consumption. Buying Juniper Networks made networking a much larger part of the company.
customers: Large enterprises, service providers, governments and research institutions.
money: standard and AI servers for data centres
switches, wireless and routing under Aruba and Juniper
storage arrays and the GreenLake consumption service
moat: Enterprise relationships and support contracts, plus networking equipment that is costly to swap once a campus or data centre runs on it.
risks: AI server sales carry very low margins because the chip cost dominates
It reported an operating loss last year after acquisition and legal charges
Debt rose to about $20 billion for the Juniper deal
Integrating two large networking businesses is a multi-year job
opportunities: Revenue grew about 14% on AI server demand
Networking is the most profitable part and is now much larger
GreenLake recurring revenue makes earnings steadier than hardware sales
watch: Networking segment margin and the AI server backlog converted into revenue.
